title: Jet Ski
text: “Anyway, now I get why Ren doesn’t seem all that bothered being in Inult form.”
“Honestly, it felt a lot like diving into the net… being in animal form, I mean.”

“No problem there. Which means Ren might actually have an aptitude for the Sword Hero role. And according to Gaelion-chan, between the sword and the spear, it was the Spear Hero—Motoyasu-kun—who ended up siding with humanity, right?”
“Well… maybe so.”
“I’ve said it many times, but I am the hero of Filo-tan, Father, and Filolial-sama, I say.”
Here, I struck the Raging Filolial-sama pose, indeed.

“The sword form Ren awakened into under Black Thunder seemed to have sharper edges than the original world’s Ren’s sword, so the Sacred Sword surely responds to a certain chuunibyou element. Turning into a monster probably isn’t the actual aptitude, I say.”
“Don’t mess around, Motoyasu! I told you I’ve graduated from that! Don’t try to steer me back toward awakening!”
That’s why Rafumi came, isn’t it! Ren shot back at me. Curses… damn you, Rafumi, indeed. The seed of Ren’s awakening has been crushed, I say.
“Anyway, here’s roughly how VR games developed in my world. Starting with Brave Star Online, all sorts of spin-off games popped up after that.”
“So simple avatar-based combat systems and the full-scale dive game Brave Star Online—that’s where VR really began.”
“There’s quite a history to it, isn’t there.”
Even the original world’s Ren had mentioned bits and pieces here and there, but never in this much detail. It really was the history of gaming, world by world, I say.
“Gaelion-chan did talk about the original Ren’s story. Though in the end it was kind of vague.”

“It was one of those ‘the man speaks through his back’ kind of stories, wasn’t it. Apparently after a bitter ending two years in, he set out again. Ren-san, do you have any idea what that might mean?”
“Not a clue. Same as our future right now, probably.”
“So all we can do is keep moving forward until we find a way back, huh. And last but not least, Motoyasu-san—if I recall, you got into gaming because a certain pig taught you how to play.”
“Indeed. As for the detailed background, all I really know is that the service started around the time online games were beginning to pop up all over the place.”

“In Motoyasu-kun’s case, it doesn’t seem all that different from the online gaming history I know. Itsuki, Ren, you two probably at least heard the general story of when online PC games first started too, right?”
Ren and Itsuki exchanged glances at Father’s explanation before both nodding.
“I know about the era before VR games, at least.”
“Same here.”

“Motoyasu-kun and I are close in era, so there probably wasn’t as dramatic a shift for us as there was for you two. I bet the Emerald Online Motoyasu-kun played was just a pretty standard online game.”
Since Father was closest to my own era, he understood things quite deeply, which I greatly appreciated, indeed.
“Naofumi-san hasn’t played a game similar to this world, but he knows a lot about all sorts of things. I’d love to hear about other online games you played, even if they weren’t like this one.”

“I’m usually the one asking about the games in this world, so… hmm, the game I played, huh. Well, it had the usual kind of backstory—monsters sealed away, a demon lord resurrecting, come fight them—but basically it was about players cooperating, dueling, and doing guild battles.”
“I imagine that’s similar for Ren-san and Motoyasu-san too. Though it sounds like Ren-san was mostly a lone wolf who soloed, occasionally dragging a junior along.”
“That’s one comment too many. You flying Riska.”
“Touched a nerve, did I… Meanwhile Motoyasu-san seems to have played with real women.”
“I played in a small guild with a bunch of pigs, I say!”
Looking back now, compared to the guilds that come up in Father’s stories, mine was small at best. Playing around like that, I could hardly claim to have fully conquered Emerald Online, indeed.

“There’s plenty I could talk about—hunting grounds, dungeons only accessible to guilds that won certain guild battles, that sort of thing—but since none of it lines up with anything here, I doubt it’s easy for you three to picture.”
“That’s fine. Naofumi-san, you’re the one who’s been listening to our stories all this time.”
“Still, I think it’s a bit different from actually adventuring through a strikingly similar world while swapping stories from our gaming days.”
Saying such things, we continued on our way, indeed. Then… we came upon what looked like some kind of waterway. On the walls were murals depicting Peckuls swimming through water, indeed.
“Just as expected. Naofumi-san, this is your moment. And while we’re at it, Motoyasu-san, why don’t you try swimming through the waterway too?”
“Leave it to me, I say!”

With a splash, I dove into the water and tried to swim, but this water… it clung to my body and dragged me down! Submarine Mode, engage! I desperately spun my spear trying to propel myself forward, but I couldn’t make any progress at all! I could run along the bottom, but even that was slower than walking on land. Argh! This is a hassle, I say! Then I’ll just cleave the water apart! With that, I swung my spear with all my might, but I couldn’t split the water at all, indeed. Glub, glub, glub… this is rough, I say! Just as I thought that, Father swam over, hooked his flippers under my arms, and hauled me up to the surface.
“*cough cough* Father, thank you very much, I say!”
“Guess you need a bit of practice.”
And with that, Father let me ride on his back and swam for me, indeed.
“Father’s Water Cruising Mode, indeed! Vroom, vroom!”
“I don’t think it’s quite like your driving mode, Motoyasu-kun. Also, could you not grab my shoulders and strike a motorcycle pose? Your hips are pressing against me in a weird spot.”
This exhilarating rush of speeding across the water’s surface was pretty wonderful, indeed. I simply had to research this Jet Ski Mode further, I say!
“Alright, I’ll go check what’s further ahead, so wait here.”

With that, Father let me off at the waterway’s edge and dove back under. He was incredibly fast—about the speed Older Sister swims at, indeed. Before long, Father came back up carrying parts of what looked like a coelacanth model.
“Just like with the needle, this might be water-but-not-quite-water. For me, just kicking my legs gets me a decent amount of speed.”
“If anything, this might be where Naofumi-san truly shines. The problem is how to deal with enemies underwater. If we run into a boss on some underwater stage, we could be in real trouble.”
“Shouldn’t we check if Itsuki and Ren can even get into the water?”
At Father’s question, Itsuki glanced over at Ren.
“I don’t mind trying, but Ren-san…”
“…I’m not getting in the water.”
Just as expected, Ren didn’t seem to have the slightest intention of getting in, indeed.
“Alright then. I’ll go ahead and dive in first.”
The moment Itsuki entered the water… his cheek pouches puffed right up.
“Itsuki… floating’s fine and all, but you need to actually dive under, don’t you?”
“N-No, it’s not that I’m trying to float. Ugh… I can’t dive. The air won’t come out of my cheek pouches!”

At that, Itsuki didn’t exactly drown, but all he managed to show us was himself swimming around with his cheeks puffed out like balloons. In the end, Father grabbed Itsuki’s leg and pulled him under, but Itsuki popped right back up to the surface immediately.
“Seems like Riska has this trait where he can float but can’t actually submerge. Some kind of gimmick meant to be used somewhere, maybe?”
“Please, have mercy. Does anyone here understand what it feels like to have your face turn into a flotation device!”
Whatever it was, it seemed to be something only Itsuki himself could truly understand, indeed.
